solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flamboyant lawyers love what Manuel says (7)

indicators.note: Manuel speaks Spanish, so the phrase asks for the Spanish word he would say for 'what'

blocks.note: love = nil = O, from tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A showy legal team and a bewildered waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel is the Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, whose catchphrase is a baffled '¿Qué?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornate seventeenth-century style of art and music gives its name to anything extravagantly showy.

clue.text: Make pale line in the sand (6)

indicators.note: 'in' places the line inside the sand, so one piece sits within the other

explanation.surface: Someone draws a line in the sand and loses their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line in the sand' is a stock phrase for a limit, so it reads as one idea; split it, and the line goes inside the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: chemically whitening cloth or hair takes the colour out of it.

clue.text: Try splitting beam of light up in practice (9)

indicators.note: to split something is to come between its parts, so the first piece sits inside the second
in a down clue, 'up' turns the letters to read bottom to top

blocks.note: a laser is a beam of light
a judge will try, or hear, a case

explanation.surface: An experiment splitting a light beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like 'attempt', but it is the courtroom sense: to hear a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors run through a play before opening night; that run-through is practice.

clue.text: Case of Ecuadorians occupying capital? Yes (5,2)

indicators.note: a case is the outside of a thing, so the word's first and last letters
to occupy a city is to be inside it, so the letters sit within the capital

blocks.note: Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A question about Ecuadorians living in their own capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is Ecuador's own, which is what makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rather formal British phrase of agreement, said where others would say yes.

clue.text: Fresh lime in tea to remove, maybe from the cup (9)

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Fishing a slice of lime out of a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The cup is a trophy, not a teacup: teams are knocked out of a cup competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A knocked-out team is removed from the cup, a sporting sense 'maybe' flags as one example.

clue.text: Issue pound, having gained backing, more or less (7)

indicators.note: the pound has something added, so the next piece comes after it
going backwards, so the assembled pair is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A currency story: sterling gains support and is roughly stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is the verb, not a problem: to put out a book or statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher issues books and papers; as verbs the two are straight synonyms.

clue.text: One’s balance improves certainly during gymnastics lesson (5)

definitions.note: a clause standing for 'one whose balance improves'

indicators.note: during means within a span of time, so the word goes within the lesson

blocks.note: PE = physical education, a school gym class

explanation.surface: A pupil's balance gets better in gym class.
explanation.walkthrough: The gymnast's balance is a bank balance: the person being paid sees their account go up.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: whoever receives a payment finds their bank balance improves.

clue.text: Area trading with rubles (7)

indicators.note: to trade is to exchange, so the letters exchange places

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: this is a country that does its trading in rubles.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: this Eastern European state's currency is the Belarusian ruble.

clue.text: Mad assessor’s self-explanatory statement? (5)

blocks.note: an assessor's job is rating, so his description of it is a two-word sentence

explanation.surface: An angry assessor explains himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I RATE and it is an assessor describing his own job; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of angry, and a two-word sentence an assessor might say of himself.

clue.text: Doubt that boy will chase mates out of bounds (8)

indicators.note: a word's bounds are its first and last letters, and those are put out

blocks.note: in the game of tag, whoever is 'it' does the chasing
mATEs without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A schoolboy chasing his friends out of the playground.
explanation.walkthrough: The playground game is the key: the one who chases is 'it', so 'that boy will chase' is HE'S IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to be unsure and waver before acting.

clue.text: Roots tangled in the densely packed place (9)

indicators.note: tangled things are twisted out of order, as the letters are

blocks.note: a city is a crowded place

explanation.surface: Tree roots tangled under a crowded city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roots' sounds botanical, but it means where a person's family comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Your roots are your ancestral and cultural origins, the group you descend from.

clue.text: See a police officer gets a round in, perhaps (5)

blocks.note: lo = see!, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: A police officer buying a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The round is a bullet, not drinks: putting a cartridge in a gun is getting a round in.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: putting a cartridge into a gun is one way of charging it, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Have a hankering for chicken, mostly (5)

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: chicken = cowardly, a six-letter synonym; 'mostly' drops its final N

explanation.surface: Someone longing for chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicken is the adjective, cowardly, not something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to long for or yearn for something.

clue.text: Really not far from home on island (2,7)

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so 'not far from home' comes after the island

explanation.surface: Living close to home on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Really' is the adverb, as in 'she meant it really', not an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: meant seriously, sincerely, not as a joke.

clue.text: In photo, auntie thanks new salesperson (4,9)

indicators.note: 'In photo' means inside the photo, so the following pieces go within it

blocks.note: an aunt is Pa's sis, father's sister

explanation.surface: An aunt in a photo thanks a new sales assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: The leap is that an aunt can be described rather than named: your father's sister, written as a possessive and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who serves customers behind a shop counter.

clue.text: Holding broken TV, consult office’s tech whizz (5,4)

indicators.note: to hold is to have inside, so the outer word holds the other letters
broken into pieces, so T and V are separated and placed apart

blocks.note: to see a doctor is to consult one
an office is a job; JOB'S

explanation.surface: Calling the office tech expert about a broken television.
explanation.walkthrough: The T and V go into SEE separately, one after each of its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apple co-founder is the best-known technology visionary of his era.

clue.text: Equally cold final section on the way up (9)

blocks.note: an ending is the final part

explanation.surface: A climb whose last stretch is just as cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a mountaineer's report, which keeps 'on the way up' looking like description rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rising or climbing.

clue.text: Game in which king swaps letter, initially for a D (8)

indicators.note: to swap is to give one thing up in exchange, so the king gives up a letter
'for' means in exchange for, so the new letters take the old one's place

blocks.note: used as is, replacing the L

explanation.surface: A word game with a king changing letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the game itself is one of acting out words syllable by syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: A party game in which players mime a word or title for others to guess.

clue.text: Poet whose children were naughty smearing earlobe with chilli (7,6)

indicators.note: smearing spreads and mixes things, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Naughty children rubbing chilli on someone's earlobe.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet wrote Cautionary Tales for Children, verses in which badly behaved children come to grisly ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by his best-known work: his comic verses are all about badly behaved children.

clue.text: Knock top off pot taken by gambler? (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top is the first letter, and it comes off

blocks.note: a gambler's take is his winnings; drop the W

explanation.surface: A gambler knocking over a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman's turn at the crease is called a knock.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang: a batsman's knock is his turn at batting.

clue.text: Well grounded soldier enters the nearest pub (7)

indicators.note: to enter a pub is to go inside it, so the soldier's letters go inside the pub's

blocks.note: your local is your nearest pub
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A sensible soldier walks into the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well grounded' looks like a description of the soldier, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument with sound grounds follows reason, so it is rational.

clue.text: Rush someone who minds taking drug (6)

indicators.note: to take a drug is to take it in, so the drug goes inside the carer

explanation.surface: Hurrying a carer who has taken drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' is a verb here: the answer is not a job but hurtling out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to hurtle along at speed, often out of control.

clue.text: Talk of the old days, short skirts in the playground back in style? (9)

indicators.note: 'in the playground' puts the skirts inside the playground's letters
the back of a word is its end, so its last letter

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground

explanation.surface: Nostalgia for miniskirts in the playground and whether they'll return to fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in style' reads as a fashion revival; it is the last letter of 'style'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to recall past times fondly, usually out loud with others.

clue.text: Singer joined then given audition (5)

indicators.note: an audition is literally a hearing, so the pieces are heard, not read

explanation.surface: A singer who joined a company after an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian double Z is said 'ts', so the word sounds like MET SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for mezzo-soprano, a female voice between soprano and contralto.

clue.text: Quality of drink that’s uncertain (5)

blocks.note: er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone unsure how good a drink is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quality' is the adjective, as in 'quality goods', not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal adjectives for first-rate, as in 'a quality meal'.

clue.text: Sail boatbuilder shortened after trimming edges for ages (5)

indicators.note: a shortened word is cut short, so it loses its final letter
the boatbuilder comes after the trimmed ages in the answer
trimming cuts off edges, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: NOAH, builder of the Ark, without his last letter

explanation.surface: A sailmaker trimming a boatbuilder's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The boatbuilder is the biblical one who built the Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jib that overlaps the mainsail, named after the Italian port.

clue.text: Nap before noon having so many hours until then (5)

explanation.surface: A morning nap with hours to go before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Then' is noon: counting from midnight, twelve hours pass until it.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve hours run from midnight to noon, and twelve is the number meant.

clue.text: Ban plagiarism in written work (9)

indicators.note: 'in written work' puts the plagiarism inside the written work's letters

blocks.note: to crib is to copy another's work

explanation.surface: A ban on copying in essays.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a school rule on copying, which hides the verb 'ban' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to forbid or outlaw officially.

clue.text: Sopranos cast short of a godfather? (7)

indicators.note: to cast is to throw, so the letters are thrown into a new order
short of means lacking, so the word goes without the A

explanation.surface: The cast of The Sopranos, the mafia TV drama, missing its godfather.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mafia godfather is a red herring: the other kind stands for a child at baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a godparent formally vouches for a child at baptism, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Classic sandcastle — Geraldine holds with symmetry (2,5)

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the phrase contains the answer
symmetry means equal on both sides, so the answer sits dead centre, six letters either side

explanation.surface: Geraldine building a perfectly symmetrical sandcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden word sits exactly in the middle of the two words, which is what 'with symmetry' promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing's five Classics are the major British flat races, and this Doncaster race is the oldest.
